title: "IOSS: Interactive Open Source Simulator"
subtitle: "Learn to contribute to research software. Play through real workflows in a safe sandbox, with humans first and LLMs as backup."
toc: false

## Why IOSS

Your first contribution to a research software project is hard.

- **The technical side:** you set up the environment, find your way in the code and understand the dependencies.
- **The social side:** you learn who does what, how issues, pull requests and reviews work, and what reviewers expect.

The documentation is often scattered. It assumes knowledge that a newcomer does not have yet. Feedback from peers and mentors is slow, so many learners ask an LLM and stop talking to people.

IOSS turns a real research software repository into a practice ground. You play the newcomer in a simulated community. Nothing that you do reaches the real project.

## How it works

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 1. The repository

A guided tour shows you the files of the project: the README, the license, the contribution guidelines. Then you set up the environment and explore the code.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 2. The community

A local Git forge runs the workflow: issue, branch, pull request, review, revision, merge. Other people play the maintainer and the reviewer. When nobody is available, a bot or an LLM plays the role.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### 3. The reflection

A shared learning notebook links each step to a learning goal. After each milestone, it asks you a question. Peers and mentors comment on your answers.
:::

:::

## Human to human first

The LLM is a stand-in and a helper. It is never the main way that people talk to each other. Peers fill the roles first. Only humans give the feedback that counts.

## Status

IOSS is a hackathon prototype. It has one practice repository, [tinystats](https://github.com/florence-bockting/tinystats), and one scenario: [your first contribution](https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS/blob/main/scenarios/first-contribution.md).

To help build IOSS, read the page [Developers](developers.qmd).

The prototype has:

- A local [Forgejo](https://forgejo.org/) sandbox with CI
- A guided tour of the repository
- A quest issue that gives you the tasks and ticks them when you finish them
